title: Lost in translation
summary: A translation app helps Tomás order dinner in Tokyo, but not in the way he hoped.
paragraphs: Tomás had prepared for his trip to Tokyo very carefully. He had a guidebook, a map, a list of temples and, most importantly, a {{translation}} app on his phone. "I don't need to learn Japanese," he told his friends. "The phone will do it for me."

On the first night he went into a small restaurant near his hotel. There were eight seats around a {{counter}} and no English on the menu. The cook smiled and waited. Tomás held up his phone and said clearly, "I would like something {{typical}}, not too spicy, please." The phone spoke in Japanese. The cook looked confused, then started laughing.

A woman at the counter helped. She spoke a little English. "Your phone said, 'I would like a normal person, not too hot,'" she explained. Everybody in the restaurant laughed, including Tomás. His face was red, but the cook made him a bowl of noodles anyway, and it was the best meal of his holiday.

After that, Tomás tried something different. Every morning he learnt five words: "thank you", "delicious", "how much", "excuse me", "where is". He wrote them on his hand. People seemed {{pleased}} when he tried, even when his pronunciation was terrible. A man at a station walked with him for ten minutes to show him the right platform.

On his last night, Tomás went back to the small restaurant. He didn't take out his phone. He said "good evening" and "delicious" in Japanese, and he pointed at what the woman next to him was eating. The cook laughed again, but this time it was a different kind of laugh. When Tomás got home, he {{signed up}} for a Japanese class.

translation.meaning: changing words from one language into another

typical.meaning: having the usual qualities of a particular thing or place

signed up.meaning: put his name on a list to join something

counter.meaning: a long table in a shop or restaurant where people are served
